vjimc-1991-01.prompt: Show that there is no arithmetic progression with three elements in the infinite geometric sequence $\{2^k\}_{k=0}^\infty$.
vjimc-1991-01.answer: If $2^k<2^l<2^m$ were in arithmetic progression, then $2^{l+1}=2^k+2^m$, i.e. $2^{l+1-k}=1+2^{m-k}$ — an odd number $\ge 3$ equal to a power of $2$, impossible.

vjimc-1991-02.prompt:
Compute the determinant
$$\det\begin{pmatrix}0&a_{12}&a_{13}&\dots&a_{1n}\\-a_{12}&0&a_{23}&\dots&a_{2n}\\-a_{13}&-a_{23}&0&\dots&a_{3n}\\ \vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\-a_{1n}&-a_{2n}&-a_{3n}&\dots&0\end{pmatrix},$$
where $n$ is an odd number.

vjimc-1991-03.prompt:
Let $[x]$ be the integer part of $x$. Find the limit
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\Big((\sqrt3+1)^n-\big[(\sqrt3+1)^n\big]\Big).$$

vjimc-1991-04.prompt: Let $f(x)$ be an even, twice continuously differentiable function and $f''(0)\ne0$. Prove that there is an extremum of $f(x)$ at the point $x=0$.
vjimc-1991-04.answer: Evenness gives $f'(0)=0$ (the one-sided difference quotients at $0$ are negatives of each other); then $f''(0)\ne0$ and the second-derivative test (Taylor with $f''$ continuous) give a strict extremum.
